readmes.cluster-release-notes:
# Cluster Release Notes

Cluster Release Notes turns deployment events and change logs into a concise summary for team review. It helps operators understand what changed, what reached the cluster, and what still needs attention.

## Features
- Collects release inputs from text files and event records
- Groups changes by service and environment
- Produces a short rollout summary for each run
- Keeps the output easy to read for on-call review

## Getting Started
Install Python, then run the script from a folder containing your input files. The tool reads local text data and writes a markdown summary to standard output. Adjust the file names and labels to match your cluster workflow.
readmes.promql-slo-notebook:
# PromQL SLO Notebook

PromQL SLO Notebook is a small command-line helper for inspecting metric snapshots and drafting service health notes. It supports repeatable checks for availability, latency, and error patterns across a cluster.

## Features
- Loads sample metric snapshots from text files
- Computes simple health scores from query results
- Formats notes for weekly review
- Keeps calculations transparent and easy to audit

## Getting Started
Install Rust, then build and run the program from the project directory. Provide one or more local input files with metric data and a target name for the scorecard output. The tool prints a plain-text summary that you can copy into your review notes.
readmes.container-workflow-scripts:
# Container Workflow Scripts

Container Workflow Scripts provides a set of small shell helpers for routine delivery work. It keeps repetitive tasks in one place so a platform engineer can run the same checks the same way each time.

## Features
- Wraps common file checks and environment setup steps
- Organizes image build and cleanup commands
- Prints clear status messages for each action
- Supports local use from a simple folder structure

## Getting Started
Use Bash to run the scripts from the project directory. Review the included command examples, adjust the folder names, and point the helpers at your local files before running a delivery task. No extra setup is needed beyond a standard shell environment.
